sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Jai Prakash Prasad,Pushkar Nath Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant Jaswant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.276 of 2021, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., P.S. Saini,
District Kaushambi during pendency of the trial.
It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Applicant is not named in the FIR.
Applicant is an old person aged about 76 years.

Named accused persons took away the photographs and Aadhar card of the applicant for the purpose of applying in old age pension scheme but they misused the photographs and documents of the applicant and executed sale deed affixing photographs.
Applicant was neither owner of the sale property nor executed any sale deed of the disputed land.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that no amount has been transferred in his account.
It is a civil dispute.

Jaswant vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150467730/
1
It is next submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that co-accused Sanjay @ Sonu
has been granted bail by coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 5.1.2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant next submits that the applicant having better case for getting bail on account of parity.
There is no prospect of trial of the present case being concluded in near future due to heavy dockets.
The applicant is not a previous convict.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.09.2022 and in case he is enlarged on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and law laid down by the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another, passed in S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Jaswant, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/ pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

Order Date :- 22.3.2023 SKD  Jaswant vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150467730/
